data.book_spec:
Genre: literary culinary thriller with magical realism
Place: Mexico City (Roma Norte restaurant; Xochimilco chinampas; San Rafael markets; government labs)
Time: present day
Theme: ambition vs. ethics; cultural stewardship; memory and food; exploitation and scarcity; science vs. tradition
Tone: sensory, tense, unsentimental, morally ambiguous
Point of View: close third on Ana Morales, occasional brief interludes from Itzel Xóchitl (first person) for contrast
Characters:  - Ana Morales, 34, chef-owner of Morada, talented, cash-strapped, disciplined - Itzel Xóchitl, 50s, chinampa farmer and guardian of a pre-Hispanic cultivation practice - Diego Ramos, 42, venture-backed investor pushing expansion - Dr. Valeria Chen, 39, food chemist at UNAM, cautious, pragmatic - Mateo Juárez, 28, sous-chef, loyal, observant - Carmen Morales, 62, Ana’s mother with early-onset Alzheimer’s - Inspector Luis Aranda, 45, health authority with a reputation for clean raids - Mikel Arriaga, 51, Basque food critic with a large platform
Premise:  - Morada is weeks from closing; suppliers demand cash; a no-star review looms. - Ana sources herbs in Xochimilco; Itzel serves her a broth infused with “flor de noche” pollen, a rare seasonal bloom cultivated on one chinampa with ritual constraints. The taste triggers sharp, specific memories; Ana’s mother briefly recognizes her after tasting a sample. - Ana builds a dish—charred quelites, amaranth aguachile, and a microdose of the pollen—that causes diners to recall vivid personal moments; word-of-mouth lines the block; Mikel’s review calls it “a memory engine.” - Diego pressures Ana to secure exclusive supply and scale; offers capital contingent on predictable output. Itzel refuses mass harvesting; warns that overuse drains the plant and unsettles “the agreements” of the chinampa.

data.enhanced_spec:
Genre: literary culinary thriller with magical realism 
Place: Mexico City (Roma Norte restaurant on Colima near Plaza Río de Janeiro; Xochimilco chinampas in San Gregorio Atlapulco, night harvests from a protected plot off the Cuemanco canal; San Rafael markets around Mercado San Cosme and Calle Serapio Rendón stalls; government labs at UNAM Instituto de Química in Ciudad Universitaria and InDRE in Tlalpan; Cofepris offices in Nápoles; Ana’s cramped walk-up in Doctores; Carmen’s public clinic near Hospital General) 
Time: present day (rainy season through Day of the Dead; water shortages, rolling brownouts, occasional canal closures after contamination alerts) 
Theme: ambition vs. ethics; cultural stewardship; memory and food; exploitation and scarcity; science vs. tradition 
Tone: sensory, tense, unsentimental, morally ambiguous 
Point of View: close third on Ana Morales, occasional brief interludes from Itzel Xóchitl (first person) for contrast 
Characters:  - Ana Morales, 34, chef-owner of Morada, talented, cash-strapped, disciplined; cooks on a scorched plancha, keeps a ledger with grease-stained notes; sleeps in the office; burns on her forearms; debt with two suppliers and back rent. - Itzel Xóchitl, 50s, chinampa farmer and guardian of a pre-Hispanic cultivation practice; speaks softly, carries a machete wrapped in cloth; maintains one ritual plot with “flor de noche”; distrusts cameras; keeps a ledger of “agreements” with the canal and birds. - Diego Ramos, 42, venture-backed investor pushing expansion; runs a ghost-kitchen portfolio; always on the phone; proposes a lab-grown “essence” deal; hides a botany grad-school dropout past. - Dr. Valeria Chen, 39, food chemist at UNAM, cautious, pragmatic; runs a small olfaction lab; files everything; knows Cofepris processes; keeps her own mother’s blood pressure pills in her desk. - Mateo Juárez, 28, sous-chef, loyal, observant; ex-baker with steady hands; sleeps on a cot after double shifts; rides a beat-up Italika; records service notes on his phone. - Carmen Morales, 62, Ana’s mother with early-onset Alzheimer’s; ex-cafeteria cook; lucid flashes triggered by smells; wanders; hums boleros when anxious; fixates on a mole recipe she can’t fully recall. - Inspector Luis Aranda, 45, health authority with a reputation for clean raids; hates theatrics; carries a laminated checklist and a reputation for not taking bribes; diabetic, never eats on raids. - Mikel Arriaga, 51, Basque food critic with a large platform; sharp palate, sharper pen; cycles the city at dawn; publishes data-heavy pieces; has a personal history with memory loss in his family. 
Premise:  - Morada is weeks from closing; suppliers demand cash; an unstarred “promising but unfocused” review from Mikel is scheduled. A compressor dies mid-service; Ana pawns her knife roll to cover ice. - In Xochimilco, Itzel serves Ana a broth infused with “flor de noche” pollen, a rare bloom harvested by moonlight when egrets settle. The taste triggers granular recall—smells of Ana’s childhood stove, her father’s aftershave. A take-home vial leads to Carmen briefly recognizing Ana and reciting, near-verbatim, a lost salsa ratio. - Ana builds a dish—charred quelites, amaranth aguachile, and a microdose of the pollen—that causes diners to recall vivid, specific personal moments. Lines form; a thread on Mexican Twitter calls it “comer recuerdos.” Mikel’s revised piece dubs it “a memory engine.”

chapters: Ana salvages a failing service by pawning her knife roll for ice and coaxing the scorched plancha back to life.
Carmen wanders and can’t place her mole while Diego corners Ana with a scaling pitch she rejects under mounting debt.
Ana hustles San Cosme and Serapio Rendón for cheap quelites and amaranth, then secures a night run with Itzel to the protected chinampa.
Itzel allows only a thumb-sized vial under strict moon-harvest rules and forbids use on closure nights, limiting access.
Ana drinks the broth, recalls her childhood stove, builds the microdosed dish, lines form, Twitter dubs it “comer recuerdos,” and Mikel revises to “a memory engine.”
Valeria flags toxicology and Cofepris review as brownouts and contamination alerts threaten the canal supply.
A crush of diners floods Morada, and Inspector Aranda grants Ana a short grace period after flagging labeling issues. (+)
Itzel rows Ana past sleeping egrets and warns her face to face that breaking moon-harvest rules ends their pact. (-)
Diego brings contracts, and Valeria agrees to characterize the pollen only under community-consent terms. (+)
While Ana plates, Diego pockets a thumb-sized vial from the lowboy and walks out. (-)
Ana, Mateo, and Itzel complete a rule-abiding night harvest under egrets and rush fresh pollen to the kitchen. (+)
Desperate on a canal-closure night, Ana rows without egrets, serves a dull batch, a guest seizes, and Cofepris halts service. (-)
Ana runs candlelit clandestine tastings to pay wages while Mateo delivers bundles to regulars and Carmen sniffs chilhuacle to spark recall. (+)
Mikel publishes a critical data piece and a viral vlog exposes Itzel’s route, drawing tourists to her chinampa. (-)
In her UNAM lab, Valeria isolates a fragile aromatic cluster and shows Ana why gentle prep preserves the effect. (+)
Diego pushes a synthetic-analog patent and a rollout plan, pressuring Ana to sign away rights. (-)
Aranda leads a clean raid, traces Diego’s pilfered vial to an export log, and confiscates it. (+)
Aranda shutters Morada for ten days and opens a formal supply-chain file on the operation. (-)
